# A data centre on every ship.

Standardised compute infrastructure on every vessel, managed through a unified fleet dashboard. Low-latency applications running where they need to, governed from shore.

## One standard across the fleet.

Every vessel in your fleet runs the same compute platform, managed through the same APIs, visible through the same dashboard. Provision VMs, push patches, take snapshots, roll back changes, and access any workstation remotely from shore.

ECDIS backup, bridge system redundancy, and any shipboard application that requires low latency and local availability. Runs on the vessel, not in the cloud.

About Seaforge

Seaforge develops offshore data-center vessels engineered to deliver reliable, high-density compute capacity where traditional infrastructure cannot. As global power constraints, interconnection delays, and regulatory friction slow the deployment of new land-based facilities, organizations face increasing difficulty expanding their digital and analytical capabilities.

Seaforge addresses these bottlenecks by shifting critical compute offshore. Each vessel integrates liquid-cooled data halls, onboard power generation, and seawater-based heat rejection, enabling large-scale deployments without dependence on constrained utility grids, freshwater resources, or long permitting cycles.

Built to government-grade security standards and designed for predictable, location-flexible deployment, Seaforge provides a scalable path to expanding national and enterprise compute capacity while reducing environmental impact and improving infrastructure resilience.

## The Mission

The maritime industry is undergoing digital transformation, but SME fleet operators are being left behind. While large shipping conglomerates invest millions in proprietary fleet management systems and predictive maintenance platforms, smaller operators who collectively control a significant portion of global tonnage lack access to these technologies. This technological gap forces them to rely on reactive maintenance schedules, inefficient routing, and manual fleet coordination, resulting in higher operational costs, increased downtime, and reduced competitiveness. Our mission is to level the playing field by making enterprise grade maritime intelligence accessible and affordable. We retrofit older vessels with modular IoT sensor systems that capture critical operational and machinery data, then combine this with our cloud-based fleet management platform. This creates a comprehensive ERP-style solution that delivers predictive maintenance alerts, optimized routing recommendations, and centralized fleet coordination capabilities that were previously exclusive to major shipping lines with dedicated IT departments.

## Powering the future with floating AI datacenters.

Bluerax is pioneering the next generation of AI datacenters by taking them offshore. We design and deliver standardized floating datacenters that solve the critical challenges of space, speed, and sovereignty in today’s compute industry.

Our modular units are built in shipyards, deployed within 12–18 months (compared to 3–5 years on land), and feature hurricane-resilient jack-up stabilization systems. Each platform integrates a closed-loop seawater cooling system, achieving 30–40% greater efficiency than conventional designs, with the option to expand into eco-enhancing solutions such as mangrove “living radiators.”

Bluerax enables governments, financial hubs, AI networks, and hyperscalers to deploy sovereign compute capacity rapidly in ports, lagoons, and coastal waters—without the land, permitting, or grid bottlenecks that slow traditional datacenter growth.

In a world where demand for AI compute doubles every year and the market is headed toward trillions, Bluerax provides a scalable, sustainable, and sovereign alternative: floating datacenters that are ready where and when they’re needed most.

Re-Architecting Hull, Mechanical & Electrical (HM&E) from the Keel Up.

We redesigned ships from first principles, starting from the engine room out. Around our engine modules, we built a fully software-defined ship with smart, modular components designed to swap out for rapid repair. Together, they become building blocks for many ships, in many shipyards, for many missions. The architecture meets and exceeds U.S. Navy requirements and is not limited to any single hull or program. Liberty Class is the first platform; the same foundation applies wherever autonomous ship operation is required.

The operating system for software-defined ships

Every sensor. Every signal. Every system. Unified. Most ship automation is proprietary and siloed. Data gets locked in OEM-controlled black boxes. AI has nothing to reason over. Open Keel is BWA's open architecture platform: the connective tissue integrating every subsystem on a vessel into a single, AI-ready data layer: propulsion, power generation, fuel management, sensors, bilges, navigation, machinery control.
